title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a group-theoretic analysis from the 'équation des lacets' manuscript, which follows on from La Longue Marche.

The ambient group M is an extended group of 'loop' type. In the surrounding pages it contains:
- a normal subgroup Π_0 (very likely the fundamental group of P^1 minus three points);
- M(0) and M^!, with M^!_0 = M(0)·Π_0;
- a map 𝔖 → 𝔖_3 together with a sign homomorphism sg : 𝔖 → μ = {±1};
- a homomorphism ε_2 : M → μ.

ρ is an element of order 3 and τ' an involution. N_ρ^* is the normaliser of ρ, Z_ρ its centraliser, and L_ρ ≅ μ × ⟨ρ⟩. D_τ' and D_ρ are small dihedral or Klein-type groups.

The previous page (diagram 37) listed the 'pieces' of N_ρ^*: finite-index subgroups lying between N_ρ^* and M^0(-j), which has index 24 = 2·2·2·3.

On this page Grothendieck redraws that lattice as a 'cube' (diagram 38).
- There are three directions of index 2: multiplying by μ, passing from M^0(-j̄) to M'(-j̄), and passing from M'(-j̄) to M'''(-j̄).
- There is one direction of index 3: adjoining ρ, i.e. passing from the '!' level to Z_ρ, N_ρ^*, L_ρ, D_ρ.
- The dashed arrows mark the index-3 extensions.

A marginal warning notes that the vertex M'(-j̄)·μ_τ' is only a product set, not a subgroup, because μ_τ' does not normalise M'(-j̄).

In section o) he turns to the finite-index subgroups of Z_ρ that appear in the cube. There are four: Z_ρ^! = M'(-j̄)×μ, Z^!_{ρ0} = M'(-j̄), M^0(-j̄)×μ, and M^0(-j̄). He asks whether they are invariant, i.e. normal, in Z_ρ.

For two of them this is clear, because they are intersections of Z_ρ with normal subgroups of M:
- M'(-j̄)×μ = Z_ρ ∩ M^!;
- M^0(-j̄)×μ = Z_ρ ∩ M^! ∩ Ker(ε_2).

The sentence continues on the next page: these two are even normal in N_ρ^*, since N_ρ^* stabilises Z_ρ, M^! and Ker ε_2.

The next page then handles M'(-j̄) using a commutator formula, [x,u] ≡ sg(x)^{ε_2(u)} mod Π_0. Since Z_ρ = L_ρ·Z_ρ^!, it suffices to check that ρ normalises it.

Overall purpose: understand the normaliser and centraliser of the order-3 element in the relevant Teichmüller / Galois–Teichmüller-type group. This means its finite-index pieces, their normality, and their quotients, presumably for use with the loop relations.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this page.
The normality argument is correct: the intersection of Z_ρ with subgroups normal in M is normal in Z_ρ. It is normal in N_ρ^* as well, because N_ρ^* normalises Z_ρ.

The cube's labelling is slightly inconsistent in the drawing. N_ρ^! is called N_ρ^? on the previous page. One mid-level vertex labelled N_ρ^* looks like a slip, perhaps for N_ρ^! or another intermediate group. Grothendieck himself flags the vertex M'(-j̄)·μ_τ' as not being a group.

ideas.what: Lattice ('cube') of finite-index subgroups between the normaliser N_ρ^* of an order-3 element and a subgroup of index 24, with index-2 and index-3 directions
ideas.modern_name: Subgroup lattice of normaliser/centraliser of a torsion element in a mapping-class / Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group theory; the context resembles the GT relations of Drinfeld and Ihara

ideas.what: Normality of subgroups proved via intersection with normal subgroups M^! and Ker ε_2
ideas.modern_name: Intersection of normal subgroups is normal

ideas.what: Remark that M'(-j̄)·μ_τ' is not a subgroup since μ_τ' does not normalise M'(-j̄)
ideas.modern_name: Product of subgroups is a subgroup iff they permute

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine bookkeeping page: a diagram of a subgroup lattice plus an elementary normality check. It is a technical step inside an unpublished computation, with no new concept or connection on the page itself.
transcription_corrections: The question reads 'sont-ils invariants dans Z_ρ ?', not 'caractéristiques'.

The second line of (39) should read M^0(-j̄)×μ ⟵(2) M^0(-j̄) = Z^{0!}_{ρ0}, matching the image. In the first line, the right-hand side should be M'(-j̄) (with the minus sign), = Z^!_{ρ0} = N^{*!}_{ρ0}.
The crossed-out text before (40) in the image is 'M^0(-j̄)×μ'. The '(40)' label precedes the brace.
The sentence continues on the next page: 'cela montre que ces groupes sont même invariants dans N_ρ^*'.
